li: FYI discovered a reproducible coherence step-down that aligns exactly with an internal KV fence boundary (64k) on q3b-int8-lite. not identical to the earlier int4 reports but looks related to cache wrap/flush. repro steps and logs below.

maya: nice find. did you run with sharded-cache on? last time shard boundaries were implicated.

li: yes sharded-cache=2, segment_size=65536. single-run notes:
```
./e2e_playback --model q3b-int8-lite --seq 90000 --seed-file tests/long/64k_trigger.txt --shards 2 --seg 65536
...
[KV] write idx=65498 len=38 seg=0
[KV] write idx=65536 len=0 seg=1  <-- zero-length write at fence
[ATTN] head0 norm abs_idx=65499 0.0041
[ATTN] head0 norm abs_idx=65500 0.0039
[ATTN] head0 norm abs_idx=65536 0.0007  <-- collapse
[METRIC] coherence 0.91 -> 0.62 at token 65540
```
looks like a race where the segment transition zeros the buffer before the transport finishes.

jonathan: interesting. this could be two separate things: (A) a transport/segment fence zeroing bug; (B) RoPE phase aliasing when absolute index jumps to next segment id and gets modulo-reduced incorrectly. can you add both debug hooks: kv_write(seq_id, abs_idx, seg_id, write_len) and rope_phase(abs_idx, computed_phase) ?

li: yep adding hooks now. quick patch: 
```diff
+ log_kv_write(seq, abs_idx, seg_id, len)
+ log_rope_phase(abs_idx, phase_val)
```
will push to bringup/kv-fence-logs.

nina: i'll spin an FP32 baseline and an int8-no-shard (seg=0) run to separate quantization vs sharding. also can we run with the runtime option "disable_kv_zero_on_rotate":true ? iirc there was a flag to avoid clearing until ack.

li: great call. i dug through transport layer and found code that does: `memset(segment_buf, 0, SEG_SZ)` immediately on rotation. probable candidate. if the transport reader can still be reading old pointers there will be a zero tail. patch idea: defer memset until reader ack or write a tombstone marker instead of clearing.

maya: in parallel i'm running a headwise RoPE check to see whether phase jumps are continuous across the fence. small python to dump phase diffs:
```python
for i, abs_idx in enumerate(range(start_idx, end_idx)):
    phase = compute_rope_phase(abs_idx)
    print(abs_idx, phase)
```
if phase has a discontinuity exactly at 65536 that's a red flag.

jonathan: also run a sanity eval: coref F1 on the list of tricky anaphora prompts. if it's a transport zeroing bug, fp32+no-shard should be fine. if it's RoPE math then all precisions will feel it but quantization may amplify.

ops-bot: scheduled job brg-kv-fence-177123 (user: nina) queued on long-run cluster (eta 12m).

li: pushed logs to bringup/kv-fence-logs branch. sample from instrumented run shows both zero write and phase continuity:
```
KV_WRITE seq=98765 abs_idx=65536 seg=1 len=0
ROPE_PHASE abs_idx=65535 phi=0.712345
ROPE_PHASE abs_idx=65536 phi=0.712351
ATTN head0 norm abs_idx=65536 0.0008
```
phase looks continuous (small float delta) which lowers probability of a RoPE math bug. suggests the zero write is the culprit.

maya: thanks. can you try adding a per-token KV re-read validation on the consumer side? if consumer reads zeros it can request a replay. small safety stop-gap: if sum(kv_buffer) < eps then flag and stall for replay. could be used as a canary while we fix transport.

li: implemented KV guard: `if kv_checksum(abs_idx) == 0: request_replay(abs_idx-64, abs_idx+64)` quick smoke: prevents coherence drop but increases tail latency by ~12%. acceptable for a mitigation.

nina: running the three-arm eval now: fp32+shard, int8+shard, int8+shard+kv-guard. will post the aggregated table but early numbers: fp32+shard coherence=0.90, int8+shard=0.61, int8+shard+guard=0.86. so guard helps a lot.

jonathan: plan: (1) land transport fix to defer memset until ack or use tombstone; (2) keep kv-guard in runtime as opt-in; (3) run full nightly across quant permutations. assign li for transport PR and maya for runtime guard. i'll file a release note for Dedicated customers pinned to this model.

li: creating PR: redwood/transport#452 defer-zero-on-rotate. test plan includes synthetic high-throughput replay to ensure no stale pointer reads.

maya: i'll prepare canary config with kv_guard=true and opt-in rollout to 10% staging first. ops-bot, can you schedule a canary deploy?

ops-bot: canary deploy queued (canary-177123-10pct), targeting q3b-int8-lite on staging.

nina: will follow up with the full eval matrix and attach diffed logs. thanks team. :raised_hands:
